title: The South Indian Kingdoms: Pallavas, Cholas, and Their Neighbours

questions.question: Which Pallava king wrote the satirical farce Mattavilasa Prahasana and began rock-cut temple building at Mandagapattu?
questions.rationale: Mahendravarman I (c. 600-630) was the scholar-king author of Mattavilasa Prahasana; his Mandagapattu temple was built 'without brick, timber, metal, or mortar' — the first rock-cut phase.

questions.question: Narasimhavarman I earned the title Vatapikonda after:
options: Capturing the Chalukya capital Vatapi in 642
questions.rationale: In 642 his general Paranjothi stormed Vatapi (Badami) and killed Pulakeshin II, earning Narasimhavarman I the title 'conqueror of Vatapi'.

questions.question: In Pallava architecture, the vimana is best described as:
options: The gateway tower of the temple
The pyramidal tower above the sanctum
questions.rationale: The vimana is the tower over the sanctum — the true crown of the temple, tallest at Thanjavur; the gopuram is the entrance gateway that later dynasties grew to record heights.

questions.question: The imperial Chola line from which the great empire grew was founded when Vijayalaya captured:
questions.rationale: Vijayalaya seized Thanjavur from the Muttaraiyar feudatories about 850 and built the Nishumbhasudani temple, reviving Chola power.

questions.question: Rajendra I took the title Gangaikonda after his expedition to:
options: The river Ganga against the Pala Mahipala I
Kandalur Salai against the Chera fleet
questions.rationale: The Gangetic expedition against Mahipala I won Rajendra the title 'conqueror of the Ganga'; he marked it with his new capital Gangaikondacholapuram and the Cholagangam tank.

questions.question: Rajendra I's naval expedition of about 1025 was directed against:
options: The Arab merchants of the Malabar coast
The kingdom of Srivijaya in Southeast Asia
The kingdom of Kotte in Sri Lanka
questions.rationale: In about 1025 Chola fleets struck Srivijaya — Palembang and Kadaram (Kedah) — to protect the merchant guilds' sea route to China.

questions.question: The Uttaramerur inscriptions describe village elections conducted by which method?
options: Show of hands in the temple
Kudavolai — drawing palm tickets from a pot
Royal nomination by the mandalam chief
questions.rationale: Under the kudavolai ('pot-ticket') system, names of qualified candidates were written on palm tickets and drawn by lot before the sabha, with term limits and an audit.

questions.question: In Chola village administration, the assembly of merchants and townspeople was called the:
questions.rationale: The nagaram was the assembly of merchants in trade centres; the ur governed ordinary villages and the sabha governed brahmadeya villages; variyams were the sabha's committees.

questions.question: The Brihadisvara temple at Thanjavur, consecrated in 1010, was built by:
questions.rationale: Rajaraja I raised the Rajarajeshvaram (Brihadisvara) between 1003 and 1010; it is one of the three UNESCO 'Great Living Chola Temples', with Gangaikondacholapuram and Darasuram.

questions.question: Under the Cholas, the land tax (kadamai) generally took what share of produce?
questions.rationale: Chola land revenue demanded roughly one-third of produce, collected in brahmadeya villages by the assemblies themselves, besides vetti (compulsory labour).
